en: You mighty men stand here!
That dark ridge running crosswise
Is no pass a mortal can cross.
Beijing, beyond the Four Companions' reach,
Is no people within our power.
When I consider the city of Beijing,
Sulayman never ruled it.
Those fierce-wrathed infidels—
None who provoked them survived.
They have many thousands of lands.
They have people of many clans.
If they surge in, bringing suffering,
Will they spare land or living soul?
They have a people called the One-Eyed.
Can a mortal face and defeat them?
From those infidels who bring misery,
Can one return here alive?
Can a man who clashes with them prosper?
Even if fought for many years,
Will the Chinese bow down?
I have many things to say.
Light was poured upon this land.
‘Until the age of Judgment Day,
No one will conquer it,’
Allah Most High, God,
Has himself spoken these words.
The last of the six lions,
If found, God's gift,
You have your lion hero Manas.
He is the champion, he is the lion.
If found, your fortune will open.
We will find Manas.
Champion Manas, the blue-maned one,
We will bind to our waists as support.
Great Manas is that lion;
He is the hero who will find your prosperity.
He will make your yurt-felt greasy.
If you meet the leopard Manas,
You handful of Muslims,
He will make you khans in every direction.
He will make your lattice walls greasy.
When he meets you,
He will make you imposing khans.
He is the high, towering mountain pass,
Whom God has allotted to us.
You handful of Muslims,
He is the hero who will care for you!
You have peoples who will be enemies.
Without letting the enemy take one hair,
You have hero Manas to care for you.
Understand, my people, heed my words.
He is the steep path, he is the mountain pass,
Whose deeds gladden the soul,
He is the precious lion Manas!
Among the Black Kalmyks in Altay
He was born.
Growing to maturity, becoming a hero,
Becoming equal to sons of heroes,
When he first perched upon a horse,
He brought uproar on the Kalmyks.
The Black Kalmyks complained;
Against Khan Esenkan himself
He unleashed great wrath, they say.
Esenkan, fearing for his throne,
Unleashed a terrible fury.
When he heard about the blood-drinker,
Khan Esenkan then,
From atop his golden throne,
Sprang flying off.
To bind the precious one,
To cast him into a pit like this,
Esenkan had made ready.
‘Bring him bound, let him not escape,’ he said,
And gathered his mighty giants, they say.
Sending his champions,
He brought an onslaught on Manas, they say.
The forty Chinese clans, that vast people,
Around the falcon sultan Manas
Had surged in and encamped, they say.
Manas is no worthless boy.
He was renowned, he was a support,
He was a lion sprung from mortals.
‘Let him become a firm protector’—
Let us rally together, Muslims!
The Creator gave him to us.
Let us fire many volleys.
If Allah Most High looks favorably,
Lion Manas, the blue-maned one,
Let us free and rescue him.
Living on safely without dying,
What inheritance would we attain?
For the blood-drinking leopard Manas,
Waging a fierce and ruinous battle,
Let us sacrifice ourselves.
If Khan Manas is found alive,
Let us gird our waists firmly.
If the Chinese are so eager,
Let us chase them as far as Beijing.
Let us bind their khans captive.
Upon the Black Chinese and Manchus,
If mighty Allah is our ally,
Let us bring havoc.
A warrior like Manas cannot be found.
Take heed, you Muslims,
A boy like Manas cannot be found!
If Manas is found alive,
Will your Manas not be a lion?
Will your Talas not be a homeland?
He will break and conquer the Afghans.
While this Manas stands,
How could a hostile people remain unharmed!
He will slaughter the Chinese for us.
He is the bold one, he is the sharp one.
If we pray, invoking Baabedin,
Manas is that peerless treasure.
He will break rock and make a road,
He will attack many lands!
When I led the army out this way,
I, your aged uncle Koshoy,
Came chewing and eating rib fat.
If the leopard Manas is found,
Not a governor's, but a khan's
Khanate I came to take.
When the whole people came out this way,
I came slicing and eating horse rump.
If cheerful Manas is found,
I came to destroy the governor-general.
Whether lying or standing, my wish—
If the generous one is found alive,
My onslaught will be worth the world!
The black spear, Zulpukor,
I mean to wield them together.
If the leopard comes into my hands,
Not merely the Chinese, but the whole world,
I mean to grapple with it.
If Khan Manas comes into my hands,
I am old Koshoy himself.
Watch, you Muslims:
Over the Black Chinese and Manchus
I shall stand as a proud khan!
Heed my words, you Muslims;
I shall bring them to obedience by my word.
The Black Chinese who heed no language,
While mighty Manas is with us,
I shall collar and subdue!
If an enemy comes out to shoot,
I shall drive him before me.
If that lion-hearted hero comes into my hands,
Not China alone, but the whole world
I shall chew between my fangs.
When my appointed death comes, I shall die.
If my mighty champion crosses my path,
If he leads an army toward China,
I shall carry his banner for him.
Beneath that banner I shall stand;
I shall serve that noble hawk.
At Chech-Töbö, standing high,
I had been dwelling at my summer pasture.
For that Manas's sake,
My adversary is Kakanchyn.
This palm-sized band of Muslims
I have brought here under guard.
My caravan brought from the crossing—
Against the accursed Black Chinese,
While my head is still free,
I have come to take revenge.
For a scattered handful of people
I shall spend my wealth;
For fortunate, heroic Manas
I shall sacrifice my life.
Your leaders and khans are here;
You are here from all the clans.
If the Chinese surge forward to attack,
If a formidable man scouts the road,
Do not lose your wits;
My people, do not flee in panic!
We shall wage a fierce struggle
Against the ill-intentioned Chinese.
Facing them and fighting,
Fierce Manas, the champion,
We shall rescue.
Those seething Chinese
Have a ridge they rely upon;
They have a place where they are entrenched.
Against bloodthirsty Manas the leopard,
Those Chinese swept in;
There they unleashed their wrath.
Sweeping down upon Manas,
To seize and bind him in combat,
To unleash their terrible wrath,
Beginning the onslaught, massing together,
They must have swept upon the bloodthirsty hero.
Swarming from every side,
The Chinese must have brought their force to bear.
After fighting for days without respite,
Manas the leopard, the bloodthirsty lion,
Must have been left under siege.
Manas must be grieving and burning,
Despairing of his precious life;
The fierce hero must have suffered.
“My blessed elder, brave Koshoy—
When will my dear elder come?” he must be saying.
If it comes into his heart, that fierce hero
Must be yearning for me.
Your champions and khans are here;
For renowned Khan Manas,
Let us face them and wage war;
Against their entrenched position
Let us fight a desperate struggle.
This is your reason to fight:
Among these Muslims who have come,
Driven into exile and misery,
There are the exiles Akbaltay and Jakyp.
To rescue them,
There is radiant Manas the lion.
One whom a man could never find by wishing,
Born from among those people,
There is radiant, generous Manas.
Do not ask what Manas is like:
He is the champion and the support;
He is the renowned, generous lion.
Without making the Kyrgyz-Burut ask,
For their scattered, diminished people,
He is both champion and guiding mind.
For the suffering Kyrgyz,
He is the master who will guard them firmly.
All my people, listen:
Against the swarming Chinese and Manchus,
Let us take on the hardship.
That solitary Manas—
Fighting without sparing our lives,
Let us rescue him.
And if God supports us,
That lion, your hero Manas,
Over the small Kyrgyz people
Let us raise him as khan.
If Manas, our support, is with us,
Against unbelievers like black spiders,
Against their heroes full of wrath,
Let us sweep in and wreak slaughter.
Against their rulers and lions,
Against Kakanchyn's people,
For Khan Manas's sake,
Let us go to war.
If we fight these Chinese,
They are a seething multitude.
If we clash with the unbelievers,
With their heroes strong of arm,
Their many rulers have their say;
Fall into their hands and the way is narrow.
They have venom that strikes like a snake.
The Chinese people are in forty divisions;
All forty follow forty different ways.
Distinguished warriors who wreck whole peoples—
They have titans and khans.
Among that people of many kinds,
